I farm 15 mu, and I have to keep the plan simple enough for my family to manage but steady enough to protect food and income. I would keep wheat-maize as my main line because I know it well, it fits my land and irrigation, and it gives me grain every year. I would put most of the land into winter wheat followed by summer maize, then keep a smaller part for cotton because it brings cash, and use peanut and mungbean on small areas to spread risk, bring in some cash, and avoid putting everything into one crop. Since I have a well, I would use irrigation where it matters most, especially for wheat and maize. I would not push inputs too hard at my age; I would use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield, keep fertilizer at moderate levels, and do enough pest control to avoid losing the crop but not spray more than needed. I would use rotary tillage on most plots because it is practical and easier to manage than deep ploughing every time.
